subject: human mouth
title: What If You Never Swallowed Your Spit?

scenes.text: What if you never swallowed your spit? You'd fill a big water bottle every day.
Your mouth makes about half a liter to one and a half liters of saliva a day, and it's ninety-nine percent water.
You swallow it without noticing, around five to seven hundred times a day, about once a minute while awake.
Spit it all out, and you lose its job: neutralizing acid and rebuilding tooth enamel with calcium and phosphate.
People with chronic dry mouth get much more tooth decay and mouth infections.
At night, saliva slows to a trickle and you swallow only a few times an hour. That's when your teeth are least protected.

description:
What if you never swallowed your spit? Adults make about 0.5 to 1.5 litres of saliva a day, and it is about 99% water. We swallow roughly 500 to 700 times a day: about once a minute awake, a few times an hour asleep.
Saliva buffers acid and supplies calcium and phosphate that rebuild enamel, so chronic dry mouth (xerostomia) raises the risk of tooth decay and fungal infections. Saliva flow drops sharply during sleep.
